statistical_content_note: operational only: freezes the batch policy that was already the default, pins the repaired batched implementation, and re-asserts the two living working documents

accepted_batch_policy.status: settled, not pending a smoke test
accepted_batch_policy.why_no_descent: the blocking condition is not batch-size-specific: batch 2 with zero padding already diverges from batch 1

batching_investigation.hypothesis: the 30/36 mismatch was caused by slicing batched generated tokens at each row's non-padding length instead of the common padded input width

evidence.test: longest row, real length == padded width (zero padding)
evidence.significance: for an unpadded row, per-row slicing and correct slicing are the same operation, so slicing cannot be the cause

evidence.test: batch-of-1 through the batched code path vs generate_exact
evidence.significance: the batched extraction, EOS trimming and decode are correct

evidence.test: batch-of-2, both rows the same prompt, pad_cells=0
evidence.result: 2/3 diverge from batch 1; row0 == row1 in 3/3
evidence.significance: no padding involved at all; the batch dimension alone suffices

batching_investigation.mechanism: changing the batch dimension changes GEMM tiling and floating-point reduction order, perturbing logits enough to flip greedy argmax at near-ties; divergence then compounds autoregressively

declined_speedup.reason: exact equivalence was not weakened to obtain a pass

defect_repaired.defect: referenced `terms`, bound only in the single-call path, so every batched call raised NameError; introduced by the A5 edit adding emitted_terminator
defect_repaired.fix: use the stop_set already bound in that scope
defect_repaired.why_no_test_caught_it: the stub batch path returns before reaching that line
defect_repaired.reason_no_impact: the batched path is unreachable under the batch-1 policy and no production run had occurred
